subject: Urgent: DPA & DocuSign hold — go‑live timeline at risk
messages:
From: Claudia Rossi <claudia.rossi@finblue.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@finblue.com
Date: 2026-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA review + KMS requirement blocking DocuSign

Marcus —

Thanks for the call this morning. Attached are our final redlines (see FinBlue_DPA_redlines_v2.pdf). Procurement is flagging your KMS language (customer-managed key requirement) as a blocker for our standard procurement path — their legal ops says they cannot accept the current subprocessor/KMS carveouts without an approved exception.

Our GC has asked for a clear timeline and whether Redwood can provide either: (a) an HSM-backed managed key option, or (b) a documented temporary exception and scope-limited addendum we can sign while that is validated.

We have a hard internal launch target of July 6. If DocuSign cannot be completed by next week the product launch will slip. Please advise next steps and who at Redwood I should speak to about the exception path.

Thanks,
Claudia
—
Claudia Rossi
Head of Procurement, FinBlue Payments
claudia.rossi@finblue.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Claudia Rossi <claudia.rossi@finblue.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-18T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA review + KMS requirement blocking DocuSign

Claudia —

Appreciate the call and the redlines. I attached a marked-up DPA with our proposed compromises and a current subprocessor snapshot (FinBlue_DPA_redlines_v2.pdf, Subprocessor_Snapshot_20260618.csv). Short answers up front:

- We can offer an HSM-backed managed key path, but the implementation and audit take ~4–6 weeks to validate.
- We can also accept an interim, scope-limited addendum to proceed with DocuSign while we complete the HSM validation — but that requires a documented risk exception signed by Redwood risk/legal and acceptance from FinBlue GC.

Internal folks looped in: Priyom (Legal) and Naomi (Risk) — can you review the redlines and advise whether we can approve a 30-day temporary exception scoped to non-production data while engineering works on HSM?

Claudia, if procurement can sign the limited addendum and accept the temporary mitigations (regional processing controls + restricted subprocessor list + immediate audit access), we will push the DocuSign envelope today. Otherwise we need an exec-level tradeoff to keep the July 6 launch.

Best,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-19T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines + KMS exception consideration (internal)

Marcus / Naomi —

Quick read of FinBlue redlines: main sticking points are (1) customer-managed KMS demand, (2) expanded subprocessor indemnity language, and (3) cross-border transfer wording. We cannot accept a blanket customer-managed key requirement for hosted customers; that needs product/infra support.

Proposed path:
- Offer managed key with HSM as our recommended default; provide timeline and milestones (engineering to confirm dates).
- Approve a 30-day temporary exception limited to staging/non‑PII traffic and explicit IP ranges, with the following mitigations: data segregation, enhanced logging, SOC2 evidence on access controls.
- Add a one-way rollback clause and an agreed review checkpoint at day 25.

I attached a subprocessor snapshot for transparency (Subprocessor_Snapshot_20260618.csv). If Naomi can sign off on the mitigations, we can present this to FinBlue as an interim option — but it will require an exec-signed risk exception on Redwood letterhead.

- Priyom
Legal Counsel — Redwood Inference
From: Claudia Rossi <claudia.rossi@finblue.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Luca Marino <luca.marino@finblue.com>, procurement@finblue.com
Date: 2026-06-20T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA review + KMS requirement blocking DocuSign

Marcus —

Understood. Procurement is insisting that we do not accept temporary exceptions without an explicit executive escalation on the Redwood side. Our GC will not sign any addendum that permits broad subprocessor changes — they need to see the mitigating controls and a signed commitment.

Can you confirm who at Redwood can provide the exec-level written exception (CISO or Head of Risk)? If we receive that plus the interim addendum today, procurement can route DocuSign for countersignature. Otherwise we will need to postpone the launch.

Thanks,
Claudia
(On Thu, Jun 18, 2026 at 10:02 AM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai> wrote:)
> Claudia —
> 
> Appreciate the call and the redlines...
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-20T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: DPA redlines + KMS exception consideration (risk note)

Marcus / Priyom —

I reviewed the proposed mitigations. I am willing to provide a conditional sign-off for a 30-day operational exception scoped as follows:

- Scope: non-production data and minimal customer metadata only; exclude sensitive PI (SSNs, account numbers) from the interim scope.
- Controls required before exception: region-restrict processing to US-only for FinBlue, immediate access logging to be forwarded to FinBlue security on request, and a formal confirmation that engineering will deliver an HSM-managed key roadmap within 30 days.
- Reporting: daily status updates to FinBlue security until HSM validation complete.

Conditional sign-off requires an exec-level approval form signed by our Head of Risk (me) and a separate note from CISO or the CRO acknowledging residual risk. I can prepare the Risk_Exception_Request_20260620.pdf and circulate for signature — but Marcus, we need to escalate so FinBlue procurement gets the documentation they require.

Naomi
Head of Risk — Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Claudia Rossi <claudia.rossi@finblue.com>
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-20T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA & DocuSign hold — proposed exec escalation and next steps

Claudia —

Thanks — good news: Naomi can provide a conditional risk sign-off pending exec acknowledgment. Next steps we propose today to avoid launch slippage:

1) Redwood will send a short, scoped interim addendum (1 page) limited to non-production data and the specific mitigations Naomi listed.
2) Naomi will sign the risk exception; we will ask our CISO to provide an acknowledgment note — both documents will be included in the DocuSign envelope.
3) FinBlue procurement to countersign DocuSign; once executed we will proceed with staging-only workloads and deliver HSM roadmap updates daily.

DocuSign envelope prepared: https://www.docusign.com/FinBlue-FB-2026-042 (placeholder until procurement confirms).

Please confirm whether procurement can accept the interim addendum and counter-sign before EOD tomorrow (2026-06-21). If yes I will push the envelope immediately and loop our CISO for the short acknowledgment. If not, we will escalate to execs for an exception decision — please advise your GC contact for that path.

Best,
Marcus
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
